stem: Under the Singapore Government's five healthcare objectives, what does the objective on personal responsibility specifically warn against over-reliance on?

options.A: MediSave and employer benefits
options.B: Private hospitals and specialists
options.C: State welfare and medical insurance
options.D: State welfare only

explanation: The objective promotes personal responsibility and cautions against over-reliance on BOTH state welfare and medical insurance. Naming only state welfare misses that medical insurance is equally flagged.

stem: The Healthcare 2020 Masterplan was launched in which year?
explanation: Despite its name, Healthcare 2020 was launched in 2012. The 2020 in the title is a target horizon, not the launch date; 2016 is when the 3 Beyonds began.

stem: MediShield Life was launched as the national basic health insurance scheme in which year?
explanation: MediShield Life launched in 2015. The year 2020 belongs to CareShield Life, which is a common confusion between the two schemes.

stem: When were the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation packages launched, respectively?

options.A: Pioneer 2012, Merdeka 2016
options.B: Pioneer 2014, Merdeka 2019
options.C: Pioneer 2015, Merdeka 2020
options.D: Pioneer 2019, Merdeka 2014

explanation: The Pioneer Generation package came first in 2014, and the Merdeka Generation package followed in 2019. Swapping the two years is the intended trap.

stem: In 2016 MOH embarked on the 3 Beyonds for Better Health, Better Care and Better Life. Which of these is one of the 3 Beyonds?

options.A: Beyond Cure to Prevention
options.B: Beyond Hospital to Community
options.C: Beyond Public to Private
options.D: Beyond Subsidy to Insurance

explanation: The three are Beyond Healthcare to Health, Beyond Hospital to Community, and Beyond Quality to Value. Beyond Hospital to Community is the correct one; the others are invented.

stem: CareShield Life is compulsory for Singaporeans born in which cohort?

options.A: 1970 or after
options.B: Before 1980
options.C: 1980 or after
options.D: 1990 or after

explanation: CareShield Life is compulsory for those born in 1980 or after, including those with pre-existing disabilities. Those born before 1980 may opt in rather than being compelled.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main types of healthcare services in Singapore?

options.A: Primary healthcare services
options.B: Dental and TCM services
options.C: Hospital services
options.D: Intermediate and Long-Term Care services

explanation: The three main types are primary healthcare, hospital services, and ILTC services. Dental, TCM and support fall under Other Healthcare Services, not the three main types.

stem: Public hospitals account for approximately what share of all hospital beds in Singapore?
explanation: Public hospitals hold about 85% of all hospital beds, leaving roughly 15% to the private sector. 50% understates the dominance of the public sector.

stem: Public hospitals in Singapore are organised into which three clusters?

options.A: NUHS, SingHealth and AIC
options.B: NUHS, NHG and NHGP
options.C: SingHealth, IHiS and NHG
options.D: NUHS, NHG and SingHealth

explanation: The three clusters are NUHS, NHG and SingHealth. The other options mix in non-cluster bodies such as IHiS and AIC.

stem: In a public hospital, a Class B1 admission is subsidised by the Government at what rate?

options.A: Up to 80%

explanation: Class B1 receives a 20% subsidy. The heavy subsidy of up to 80% applies to B2 and C wards, while Class A gets none.

stem: Under Flexi-MediSave, how much may a senior use per year for outpatient treatment at public healthcare institutions and CHAS GP clinics?
explanation: Flexi-MediSave allows an additional S$300 per year. The S$700 figure is the separate annual withdrawal cap for outpatient treatment of the 23 chronic conditions.

stem: Healthier SG shifts healthcare cluster funding from a workload-based model to which model?

options.A: Means-tested model
options.B: Reimbursement model
options.C: Capitation-based model
options.D: Fee-for-service model

explanation: Healthier SG moves clusters to a capitation-based funding model, with each cluster caring for about 1.5 million residents. Fee-for-service is closer to the old workload-based approach it replaces.

stem: Under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), what do the different card colours signify?

options.A: The type of chronic condition covered
options.B: The patient's ward class entitlement
options.C: The patient's citizenship status
options.D: The subsidy tier the holder qualifies for

explanation: CHAS card colours (Blue, Orange, Green) indicate the subsidy tier. They are not tied to ward class or a specific condition.

stem: Health Insurance provides financial benefits in three categories. Which of the following is one of them?

options.A: Reimbursement of medical treatment or care cost
options.B: A savings return on invested premiums
options.C: A discount on future hospital admissions
options.D: A tax rebate on medical expenses

explanation: The three categories are reimbursement of cost, periodic income on disability or hospitalisation, and a lump sum on disability or major illness. Investment returns and tax rebates are not among them.

stem: Medical Expense Insurance is also commonly known by which name?

options.A: Hospital and Surgical (H&S) Insurance
options.B: Critical Illness Insurance
options.C: Permanent Health Insurance
options.D: Managed Care Insurance

explanation: Medical Expense Insurance is also called Hospital and Surgical (H&S) Insurance. Permanent Health Insurance is the alternate name for Disability Income Insurance.

stem: For accident inpatient dental treatment to restore sound natural teeth to be claimable, the treatment must be received within how many days following the accident?

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 31 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 60 days

explanation: Accident inpatient dental treatment must be received within 31 days of the accident. The 90-day figure is the typical claim notification period, not the treatment window.

stem: For a living donor organ transplant benefit, the recipient's organ failure must first be diagnosed after a waiting period of how long?

options.A: 24 months
options.B: 12 months
options.C: 36 months
options.D: 6 months

explanation: The recipient's failure must be first diagnosed after a 24-month waiting period, and the recipient must be the insured's family member. A 12-month period is a common look-back for pre-existing conditions, not this benefit.

stem: Regarding outpatient cancer coverage, which statement is correct?

options.A: Cancer drug treatment must be on the CDL, but cancer drug services are payable even for non-CDL treatments
options.B: Both cancer drug treatment and services are payable only if on the CDL
options.C: Neither cancer drug treatment nor services need to be on the CDL
options.D: Cancer drug services must be on the CDL, but drug treatment need not be

explanation: Cancer drug TREATMENT must be on the Cancer Drug List, whereas cancer drug SERVICES are payable even for non-CDL treatments. The distinction between treatment and services is the key.

stem: How does Medical Expense Insurance differ from life insurance in terms of recovery?

options.A: A policyholder cannot recover the same medical expense from multiple policies
options.B: Recovery is always paid as a fixed lump sum regardless of cost
options.C: A policyholder can recover the same expense from multiple policies
options.D: Recovery is guaranteed even without proof of expense

explanation: Being a reimbursement contract, the same medical expense cannot be double-recovered from multiple Medical Expense policies. Life insurance sums assured, by contrast, can stack across policies.

stem: Deductibles under an Integrated Shield Plan are typically tiered so that:

options.A: The deductible is the same across all ward classes
options.B: The higher the Class of Ward, the higher the deductible
options.C: The higher the Class of Ward, the lower the deductible
options.D: Only private hospital stays carry a deductible

explanation: The deductible rises with ward class, e.g. Class C at S$1,500 up to Class A and private at S$3,500. This encourages appropriate ward selection.

stem: Which type of deductible is described as the most restrictive because it must be borne for each claim regardless of policy year?

options.A: Per annum deductible
options.B: Per disability (per year) deductible
options.C: Per disability (per claim) deductible
options.D: Lifetime deductible

explanation: The per disability (per claim) deductible is the most restrictive, applying to every claim. The per annum deductible is the most common and generous, since all eligible expenses in the year count toward it.

stem: Co-insurance requires the policy owner to pay a specified percentage of which amount?

options.A: The total hospital bill before any deductible
options.B: The covered medical expenses in excess of the deductible
options.C: The deductible amount itself
options.D: The annual limit of the policy

explanation: Co-insurance is charged on covered expenses ABOVE the deductible, not on the whole bill. Applying it to the full bill before deductible overstates the policyholder's share.

stem: Under a family policy, how does the deductible apply across insured members?

options.A: The deductible applies separately to each insured member
options.B: The deductible is halved for each additional member
options.C: Only the policy owner bears a deductible
options.D: Members can combine expenses to satisfy one shared deductible

explanation: The deductible applies separately to each insured family member, so a husband cannot combine his expenses with his wife's to satisfy it. There is no shared or pooled deductible.

stem: When is a pro-ration factor applied to reduce the benefit payable?

options.A: When the insured is admitted to a ward higher than the plan entitlement
options.B: When the insured resides overseas
options.C: When the insured is admitted to a ward lower than the plan entitlement
options.D: When the insured makes more than one claim in a year

explanation: Pro-ration applies when the insured chooses a hospital or ward higher than the plan entitlement, reflecting lost Government subsidy. Choosing a lower ward does not trigger it.

stem: The 'event limit' under a Medical Expense Insurance policy refers to the maximum payable:

options.A: Per disability or illness under a single claim
options.B: Per day of room and board
options.C: Over the insured's lifetime
options.D: Per calendar or policy year

explanation: The event limit caps the amount payable per disability or illness under one claim. The lifetime limit spans the insured's life and the annual limit spans a year.

stem: A waiting period under a Medical Expense Insurance policy does NOT apply to which of the following?

options.A: Pre-existing conditions
options.B: Accidental injury
options.C: Maternity benefits
options.D: Specified illnesses

explanation: Accidental injury is covered immediately, so no waiting period applies. Waiting periods may still apply to pre-existing conditions and maternity.

stem: Regarding renewability, which statement about Integrated Shield Plan policies is correct?

options.A: They cannot be renewed after age 65
options.B: Renewal is at the insurer's discretion each year
options.C: Renewal requires fresh underwriting annually
options.D: They are guaranteed renewable

explanation: All IP policies are guaranteed renewable, so the insurer cannot decline renewal based on claims or health. Premiums are still age-banded and adjustable with notice.

stem: Which of the following is generally NOT excluded under a Medical Expense Insurance policy?

options.A: Self-inflicted injury
options.B: Cosmetic surgery
options.C: Injury while a fare-paying passenger on a scheduled commercial flight
options.D: Treatment of drug addiction

explanation: Travel as a fare-paying passenger on a scheduled commercial flight is not excluded; only non-scheduled or hazardous flying is. Cosmetic surgery, self-inflicted injury and drug addiction treatment are all excluded.

stem: The Co-ordination of Benefits Clause ensures that:

options.A: The insured must claim from the cheapest insurer first
options.B: Benefits are doubled if two policies apply
options.C: Pre-existing conditions are automatically covered
options.D: Total claims cannot exceed total actual medical expenses incurred

explanation: The clause prevents total benefits from exceeding actual expenses; payment from other sources like an employer's Group H&S reduces the insurer's payable amount. It is a limitation, not a doubling of benefits.

stem: Which form is the main underwriting source for GROUP medical cover?

options.A: The Notice of Assessment
options.B: The Group Insurance Fact-Finding (GIFF) Form
options.C: The individual proposal form
options.D: The Clinical Abstract form

explanation: For group cover the employer completes the GIFF Form. The individual proposal form is the source for individual cover.

stem: For acute inpatient care in a public hospital, who is NOT entitled to any Government subsidy?

options.A: Foreigners
options.B: Merdeka Generation seniors
options.C: Singapore Permanent Residents
options.D: Singapore Citizens

explanation: Only Citizens and PRs receive subsidies, with Citizens always subsidised more than PRs. Foreigners receive no Government subsidy.

stem: Under MAS Notice 117, what is the minimum structured CPD training on MediShield Life or shield plan content required before each calendar year end?

options.A: 4 hours
options.B: 8 hours
options.C: 1 hour
options.D: 2 hours

explanation: MAS 117 requires a minimum of 2 hours of structured CPD on shield plan content per calendar year, with records kept for 5 years.

stem: Which termination condition applies to GROUP Medical Expense policies but not individual ones?

options.A: Death of the insured
options.B: Reaching the lifetime limit
options.C: Expiry of the last paid premium period
options.D: Cessation as an employee

explanation: Cessation as an employee is a group-only termination trigger. Death, lifetime limit and premium expiry apply to both individual and group policies.

stem: Charlie holds a Medical Expense policy with a per annum deductible of S$2,000 and 20% co-insurance. Earlier in the year he already incurred S$1,000 of eligible expenses that were within the deductible. He is now admitted with a S$5,000 bill fully within his policy limits. How much will the insurer pay for this admission?
explanation: Remaining deductible is S$2,000 minus the S$1,000 already met, i.e. S$1,000. Claimable is S$5,000 minus S$1,000 = S$4,000; co-insurance of 20% is S$800, so the insurer pays S$3,200. S$4,000 forgets the co-insurance step.

stem: A policy has a per annum deductible of S$3,500 and 10% co-insurance. The insured's covered hospital bill is S$8,400 (already fully within limits and no pro-ration applies). How much does the insurer pay?
explanation: After the S$3,500 deductible, S$4,900 remains; co-insurance of 10% is S$490, so the insurer pays S$4,900 minus S$490 = S$4,410. S$4,900 ignores the co-insurance deduction.

stem: An insured entitled to a standard B1 ward is admitted to a private hospital. Covered charges are S$24,000, the pro-ration factor is 35%, the annual deductible is S$3,500 and co-insurance is 10%. What is the benefit the insurer pays?
explanation: Pro-ration first: 35% of S$24,000 = S$8,400. Subtract the S$3,500 deductible to get S$4,900, then subtract 10% co-insurance (S$490) to reach S$4,410. Using S$24,000 without pro-ration gives the wrong, inflated figures.

stem: A key eligibility criterion for Group Insurance is that the group must:

options.A: Be a registered company only
options.B: Have all members individually underwritten
options.C: Have been formed for a purpose other than obtaining insurance
options.D: Consist of at least 100 members

explanation: The group must exist for a purpose other than buying insurance, such as a company or trade union. You cannot assemble a group solely to obtain cover.

stem: In Group Insurance, experience-rating means the premium is priced based on:

options.A: The group's own past claims history
options.B: Each member's individual medical history
options.C: The insurer's overall portfolio claims
options.D: Industry-wide standard tables only

explanation: Experience-rating prices the group on its own past claims. It does not rely on individual member histories or a fixed industry table.

stem: Under the actively-at-work clause, an employee who is on annual leave on the day coverage takes effect will:

options.A: Have coverage backdated automatically
options.B: Not be covered until actively at work
options.C: Be covered only for accidents
options.D: Be covered as normal

explanation: The clause requires the employee to be actively at work on the effective day; being on annual leave (or sick leave) means no cover until they return. It is not limited to sick leave.

stem: How is the premium for Group Insurance typically described compared with individual insurance?

options.A: Unit-related and lower
options.B: Fixed regardless of group size
options.C: Age-related and lower
options.D: Age-related and higher

explanation: Group premiums are unit-related and generally lower, while individual premiums are age-related and higher. The group is underwritten as a whole rather than per person.

stem: A voluntary (contributory) group plan usually requires a minimum participation rate of about:
explanation: Voluntary plans typically require about 75% minimum participation. A compulsory plan by contrast requires 100% of eligible employees, with the employer paying all premiums.

stem: In a compulsory (non-contributory) group plan, the premium is paid by:

options.A: Split equally between employer and employees
options.B: The employees solely
options.C: The insurer as a subsidy
options.D: The employer solely

explanation: A compulsory plan is non-contributory, so the employer pays all premiums and all eligible employees are covered. In a voluntary plan employees may pay part of the premium.

stem: From which date were Government subsidies on hospital bills for foreigners removed?

options.A: 1 January 2004
options.B: 1 October 2020
options.C: 1 July 2023
options.D: 1 January 2008

explanation: Foreigner hospital subsidies were removed from 1 January 2008, after which MOM required employers to maintain medical insurance for foreign workers. 1 April 2004 relates to portable medical benefits.

stem: Under the enhanced migrant worker medical insurance (Stage 1 from 1 July 2023), for claim amounts above S$15,000 the co-payment split between insurer and employer is:

options.A: Insurer 75%, employer 25%
options.B: Insurer 25%, employer 75%
options.C: Insurer 90%, employer 10%
options.D: Insurer 50%, employer 50%

explanation: Above S$15,000 the insurer pays 75% and the employer co-pays 25%, with an annual claim limit of at least S$60,000. Reversing the split is the trap.

stem: For a Work Permit holder (excluding migrant domestic workers), any co-payment arrangement must not exceed what proportion of the employee's monthly salary?
explanation: The co-payment cannot exceed 10% of monthly salary and must not run beyond six months for every two years of employment. Migrant domestic workers are excluded from such arrangements.

stem: Employers who implement a portable medical benefits option can claim a higher tax deduction for medical expenses of up to what percentage of total employees' remuneration?
explanation: Portable options raise the deduction cap to 2% of total remuneration; without them the deduction stays at 1%.

stem: Under the Portable Medical Benefits Scheme (PMBS), what does the employer do?

options.A: Buys a Group H&S policy on the employee's behalf
options.B: Makes additional monthly contributions to the employee's MediSave account
options.C: Reimburses hospital bills as they arise
options.D: Pays cash medical allowances directly to staff

explanation: Under PMBS the employer contributes to the employee's MediSave, which the employee uses to pay MediShield Life or IP premiums, so cover follows the person between jobs. It is not a group policy purchase.

stem: To qualify for the 2% tax deduction under PMBS, for full-time employees the employer must contribute at least 1% of gross monthly salary subject to a monthly minimum of:
explanation: The minimum contribution is S$16 per calendar month for full-time employees. The employer must also cover at least 20% of local employees.

stem: The Transferable Medical Insurance Scheme (TMIS) extends inpatient coverage for up to how long when an employee leaves employment?

options.A: 6 months
options.B: 24 months
options.C: 3 months
options.D: 12 months

explanation: TMIS continuation of coverage lasts up to 12 months after the employee leaves. The 6-month figure relates to migrant worker co-payment duration, not TMIS.

stem: To qualify for TMIS, the employer must have a group of at least how many employees?

options.A: 50 or more
options.B: 5 or more
options.C: 11 or more
options.D: 20 or more

explanation: TMIS requires 11 or more employees and at least 50% of local employees insured (minimum 11), with the employer paying 100% of the GHS premium. The 20% figure applies to PMBS coverage, not TMIS.

stem: If an employee is hospitalised for a pre-existing condition within the first 12 months under a new TMIS employer's plan, the entitlement paid is:

options.A: Always the new employer's plan
options.B: The higher of the new or prior employer's plan
options.C: Nil, as pre-existing conditions are excluded
options.D: The lower of the new or prior employer's plan

explanation: During the first 12 months the employee receives the LOWER of the two employers' TMIS entitlements for a pre-existing condition. It is neither excluded outright nor defaulted to the new plan.

stem: Which of the following is NOT an eligible benefit under TMIS?

options.A: In-hospital doctor's visits
options.B: Daily room and board
options.C: Outpatient kidney dialysis or cancer treatment
options.D: ICU charges

explanation: Outpatient kidney dialysis and cancer treatment are not eligible under TMIS, along with pre/post-hospitalisation outpatient and emergency outpatient accident. Room and board, ICU and in-hospital visits are eligible.

stem: A key structural difference between PMBS and TMIS is that:

options.A: Both expire 12 months after termination
options.B: Neither continues once the employee leaves the job
options.C: PMBS coverage can be lifetime while TMIS expires at statutory retirement age
options.D: TMIS coverage can be lifetime while PMBS expires at retirement age

explanation: PMBS coverage (via an IP) can be lifetime, whereas TMIS coverage expires at statutory retirement age or 12 months after termination. The two are commonly reversed.

stem: The additional tax deduction for ad-hoc MediSave contributions is subject to a limit per employee per year of:
explanation: Ad-hoc MediSave contribution deductions are capped at S$2,730 per employee per year, within an overall 2% deduction ceiling. S$16 is the PMBS monthly minimum, not this cap.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage specific to a compulsory (rather than voluntary) group plan?

options.A: Greater risk pooling and employer control of benefits
options.B: Employees can choose whether to be insured
options.C: Lower premiums than buying individually for volunteers
options.D: Employees share the cost of premiums

explanation: Compulsory plans give greater risk pooling and stronger employer control of the benefit structure. Cost-sharing and employee choice are features of voluntary plans.

stem: A migrant worker's hospital claim under the enhanced (Stage 1) scheme totals S$35,000. Above the S$15,000 threshold the insurer pays 75% and the employer 25%. Ignoring the annual limit, how much does the employer co-pay on the portion above S$15,000?
explanation: The amount above S$15,000 is S$20,000; the employer's 25% share is S$5,000 and the insurer covers 75% (S$15,000). S$8,750 wrongly applies 25% to the whole S$35,000 bill.

stem: Disability Income Insurance is also known as Permanent Health Insurance because:

options.A: It covers permanent disabilities only
options.B: Premiums remain permanently level
options.C: The insurer cannot cancel it no matter how many claims are made
options.D: It pays a permanent lump sum

explanation: It is called Permanent Health Insurance because the insurer cannot cancel it regardless of the number of claims. It pays monthly income, not a permanent lump sum.

stem: Which statement best distinguishes Disability Income Insurance from Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) cover?

options.A: DII pays monthly income pegged to salary; TPD pays a lump sum not pegged to salary
options.B: DII pays a lump sum; TPD pays monthly income
options.C: TPD is available only to those with earned income
options.D: Both are pegged to salary and pay monthly

explanation: DII pays monthly income pegged to salary (up to 75%) and needs earned income; TPD pays a lump sum, is not salary-pegged, and can cover non-workers. The roles of lump sum and monthly income are reversed in the trap.

stem: The disability benefit is generally allowed to cover only up to what percentage of the insured's average income over the past 12 months?
explanation: The benefit is capped at 75% of past 12 months' average income; a self-employed person may get a lower percentage such as 60%. Capping below 100% preserves the incentive to return to work.

stem: Under the 'Own Occupation' definition, total disability means the insured is unable to:

options.A: Perform any occupation whatsoever
options.B: Perform three of the six ADLs
options.C: Perform the material duties of his own occupation
options.D: Perform any occupation he is reasonably suited for

explanation: Own Occupation, the most generous definition, keys on inability to perform the material duties of the insured's own job. The other definitions are Modified Own Occupation, Any Occupation and the ADL-based severe disability test.

stem: Ranked from most generous to most restrictive, the total disability definitions are:

options.A: Own Occupation, Modified Own Occupation, Any Occupation
options.B: Own Occupation, Any Occupation, Modified Own Occupation
options.C: Modified Own Occupation, Own Occupation, Any Occupation
options.D: Any Occupation, Modified Own Occupation, Own Occupation

explanation: Own Occupation is the most generous, Modified Own Occupation is stricter (it includes similar occupations), and Any Occupation is the hardest to claim under.

stem: Under the 'Severe Disability' definition borrowed from LTC, the insured must be unable to perform at least how many of the six Activities of Daily Living?

options.A: Four
options.B: Three
options.C: One
options.D: Two

explanation: Severe disability requires inability to perform at least three of the six ADLs. This definition is used during non-working periods with a fixed, lower benefit.

stem: Partial disability generally applies when the insured returns to some work but earns:

options.A: More than pre-disability earnings
options.B: At least 90% of pre-disability earnings
options.C: 75% or less of pre-disability earnings
options.D: Exactly 100% of pre-disability earnings

explanation: Partial disability requires income to fall to 75% or less of pre-disability earnings, i.e. at least a 25% drop. Earning near or above the old salary would not qualify.

stem: For recurrent disability from the same cause, most insurers waive the deferred period if relapse occurs within about:

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: 365 days
options.D: 180 days

explanation: A relapse from the same cause within roughly 180 days is treated as a continuation, so the deferred/elimination period is waived and payments resume immediately.

stem: Which combination of features will LOWER the premium of a Disability Income policy?

options.A: Shorter deferred period and longer benefit period
options.B: Shorter deferred period and shorter benefit period
options.C: Longer deferred period and shorter benefit period
options.D: Longer deferred period and longer benefit period

explanation: A longer deferred period delays payout and a shorter benefit period limits payout duration, both reducing the premium. Shortening the deferred period or lengthening the benefit period raises cost.

stem: Which of the following would generally make an insured INELIGIBLE for disability benefit payment?

options.A: Being between jobs when disabled
options.B: Keeping the policy in force
options.C: Being disabled past the deferred period
options.D: Residing outside Singapore beyond about six months

explanation: Residing overseas beyond roughly six months breaches eligibility. Being between jobs is expressly allowed, and remaining disabled past the deferred period is a condition FOR payment.

stem: Under the Limitation of Disability Benefit Clause, which of the following is EXCLUDED from reducing the monthly benefit?

options.A: Continuing salary from the insured's occupation
options.B: Work Injury Compensation payments
options.C: Benefits from another disability income policy
options.D: TPD benefits under a Life policy

explanation: TPD benefits under Life policies are excluded from the reduction, whereas Work Injury Compensation, continuing salary and other disability policies do reduce the benefit.

stem: Which statement about the features of a Disability Income Insurance policy is correct?

options.A: Benefits are taxable as income
options.B: It has a surrender value and can be assigned
options.C: It can be issued as a third-party policy
options.D: It has no surrender value, cannot be assigned, and its benefits are non-taxable

explanation: The policy has no surrender value, cannot be assigned, is not a third-party policy, and its benefits are non-taxable, with a 30-day grace period. Assignability and taxability are the tempting wrong statements.

stem: A self-employed applicant for Disability Income Insurance is typically asked to provide the Notice of Assessment or audited accounts covering how many years?

options.A: Six years
options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: One year

explanation: Self-employed applicants provide three years of Notice of Assessment or audited accounts. Salaried employees typically provide six months of CPF statements or a Notice of Assessment.

stem: Under occupation rating for Disability Income Insurance, musicians and authors are typically classified as:

options.A: Decline (uninsurable)
options.B: Class I (standard rating)
options.C: Class III (light skilled manual)
options.D: Class IV (semi/unskilled manual)

explanation: Musicians and authors fall under Decline (uninsurable) due to variable income and risk profile. Class I is reserved for sedentary indoor professions like accountants and doctors.

stem: A pregnancy-related disability under a Disability Income policy is generally payable only if the disability:

options.A: Continues more than 90 days after termination of the pregnancy
options.B: Is diagnosed within 31 days of delivery
options.C: Results in inability to do one ADL
options.D: Occurs during the pregnancy itself

explanation: Pregnancy-related disability pays only if it persists more than 90 days after the pregnancy ends, deemed to start at day 90. Disability during the pregnancy itself is excluded.

stem: Insurers usually issue Group Disability Income Insurance only if the employer already holds which policy with them?

options.A: A Work Injury Compensation policy
options.B: An Integrated Shield Plan
options.C: A Group Hospital and Surgical policy
options.D: A Group Term Life Insurance policy

explanation: A Group Term Life Insurance policy is a prerequisite; Group DII is issued alongside it or as a rider to it. A Group H&S policy is not the stated precondition.

stem: For a Disability Income claim, the insured must typically notify the insurer within how many days of the disability's commencement?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 180 days

explanation: The DII claim notification example is within 60 days of commencement. Note this contrasts with Medical Expense Insurance's 90-day notification window.

stem: A salaried employee earned an average of S$6,000 per month over the 12 months before disability. Applying the standard maximum income-replacement ceiling, what is the highest monthly benefit an insurer would normally allow?
explanation: The maximum is 75% of S$6,000, which is S$4,500. S$3,600 wrongly uses 60% (the self-employed rate) and S$6,000 wrongly assumes full replacement.

stem: Larry earned S$8,000 a month before disability and received a total disability benefit of S$6,000. He later takes a job paying S$1,000 a month. Using the partial disability formula, what monthly benefit will the insurer now pay?
explanation: Benefit = (8,000 minus 1,000) / 8,000 x 6,000 = 7/8 x 6,000 = S$5,250. Adding his S$1,000 pay gives S$6,250 total, still below his original S$8,000. S$6,000 ignores the partial reduction.

stem: Eddy is insured for a monthly benefit of S$6,000 with a 3% per annum escalation benefit. After one full year of continuous disability, what is his escalated monthly benefit?
explanation: 3% of S$6,000 is S$180, so the escalated benefit is S$6,000 plus S$180 = S$6,180. S$6,300 wrongly applies 5%, and S$6,000 forgets to escalate.

stem: How does Long-Term Care (LTC) Insurance interact with other health policies such as MediShield Life and Critical Illness Insurance?

options.A: It only pays if the others have been exhausted
options.B: It pays in addition to them
options.C: It reduces their payouts proportionally
options.D: It replaces them entirely

explanation: LTC Insurance pays in ADDITION to policies like MediShield Life, Hospital Income and Critical Illness cover, meeting care costs those policies generally exclude. It is not a replacement or a top-up-only benefit.

stem: Which describes a 'disability-based' LTC policy?

options.A: It reimburses actual home-care costs only
options.B: It pays only when the insured uses a covered care service
options.C: It pays a pre-agreed amount for each service used
options.D: It pays when the insured meets a disability trigger such as advanced dementia or significant ADL loss

explanation: A disability-based policy pays on a disability trigger (advanced dementia, significant ADL limitation, loss of intellectual capacity) regardless of service used. Service-based policies instead pay when covered services are used.

stem: Which of the following is one of the six Activities of Daily Living used in LTC assessment?

options.A: Transferring
options.B: Shopping
options.C: Managing finances
options.D: Cooking

explanation: The six ADLs are washing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility and transferring. Cooking, shopping and managing finances are instrumental activities, not the six ADLs.

stem: For advanced dementia to qualify under LTC Insurance, it must arise from:

options.A: Any stress-related condition
options.B: An organic disorder such as Alzheimer's
options.C: A temporary post-surgery confusion
options.D: Neurosis or a psychiatric illness

explanation: Advanced dementia must stem from an organic cause such as Alzheimer's or an irreversible organic disorder. Neurosis and psychiatric illness are expressly excluded.

stem: The standard deferred period before LTC benefits become payable, measured from the first day of continuous inability to perform ADLs, is:

options.A: 90 days
options.B: 180 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: 30 days

explanation: Most LTC insurers apply a 90-day deferred period so that short-term post-hospital dependence does not trigger a claim.

stem: The small death benefit under an LTC policy is typically indicated at S$5,000 up to a maximum of:

options.A: Three times the LTC monthly benefit
options.B: Six times the LTC monthly benefit
options.C: The full sum assured
options.D: Ten times the LTC monthly benefit

explanation: The LTC death benefit is small, indicatively S$5,000 up to six times the monthly benefit, and cover ceases once it is paid.

stem: ElderShield was first introduced in 2002 as ESH300. What monthly payout and maximum duration did ESH300 provide?

options.A: S$600 for life
options.B: S$300 for up to 72 months
options.C: S$400 for up to 72 months
options.D: S$300 for up to 60 months

explanation: ESH300 paid S$300 per month for up to 60 months (5 years). The S$400 for 72 months figure belongs to the 2007 ESH400 upgrade.

stem: Following the 2007 review, ElderShield 400 (ESH400) paid a monthly benefit of:

options.A: S$400 for up to 72 months
options.B: S$400 for up to 60 months
options.C: S$600 for up to 72 months
options.D: S$300 for up to 60 months

explanation: ESH400 paid S$400 per month for up to 72 months (6 years). ESH300 was the earlier S$300 for 60 months version.

stem: From which date did the Government take over the administration of ElderShield from private insurers?

options.A: 1 January 2020
options.B: 1 November 2021
options.C: 1 October 2020
options.D: 1 December 2021

explanation: The Government took over ElderShield administration from 1 November 2021. The 1 October 2020 date is when CareShield Life and MediSave Care launched.

stem: Auto-enrolment ages differ between the two schemes. ElderShield auto-enrolled eligible persons at what age, and CareShield Life at what age?

options.A: ElderShield 40, CareShield Life 30
options.B: ElderShield 30, CareShield Life 40
options.C: Both at age 30
options.D: Both at age 40

explanation: ElderShield auto-enrolled at age 40; CareShield Life auto-enrols at age 30. Swapping the two ages is the trap.

stem: What is the ADL trigger for claiming under ElderShield?

options.A: Inability to perform one of the six ADLs
options.B: Inability to perform all six ADLs
options.C: Inability to perform three of the six ADLs
options.D: Inability to perform two of the six ADLs

explanation: An ElderShield claim requires an MOH-accredited assessor to certify inability to perform three of the six ADLs. This same 3-of-6 trigger applies to CareShield Life and MediSave Care.

stem: The cost of a severe disability assessment for an ElderShield claim is S$100 for a clinic assessment and how much for a house call?
explanation: A house-call assessment costs S$250 versus S$100 at a clinic; the full fee is reimbursed with the first payout if the person is assessed as severely disabled.

stem: CareShield Life officially launched on which date?

options.A: 1 November 2021
options.B: 1 December 2021
options.C: 1 January 2020
options.D: 1 October 2020

explanation: CareShield Life launched on 1 October 2020. 1 November 2021 is when the Government took over ElderShield administration.

stem: CareShield Life pay-outs started at what monthly amount in 2020, increasing annually until age 67 or a successful claim?
explanation: CareShield Life pay-outs began at S$600 per month in 2020, rising annually until age 67 or a successful claim, and are paid for the entire duration of disability. S$400 is the ESH400 figure.

stem: A distinguishing feature of CareShield Life compared with ElderShield is that its pay-outs are:

options.A: Capped at 72 months
options.B: Paid only as a one-time lump sum
options.C: Made for the entire duration the insured remains severely disabled
options.D: Capped at 60 months

explanation: CareShield Life pays for life as long as the insured stays severely disabled, unlike ElderShield's capped 60 or 72 month terms. It is not a lump-sum benefit.

stem: Under MediSave Care, what is the maximum monthly cash withdrawal, and what minimum MediSave balance is required to qualify for that maximum?

options.A: S$150 per month, balance of S$15,000 or more
options.B: S$200 per month, balance of S$20,000 or more
options.C: S$200 per month, balance of S$10,000 or more
options.D: S$300 per month, balance of S$20,000 or more

explanation: The maximum MediSave Care withdrawal is S$200 per month, available only with a balance of S$20,000 or more. A balance below S$5,000 means no withdrawal is available.

stem: For those born 1979 or earlier who join CareShield Life, the participation incentive of up to S$3,000 is available if they join by:

options.A: 31 December 2023
options.B: 31 December 2024
options.C: 31 December 2025
options.D: 31 December 2021

explanation: The up-to-S$3,000 incentive, spread over 10 years, applies to those joining by 31 December 2024. 31 December 2023 was the opt-out deadline for certain 1970-1979 cohorts, not the incentive date.

stem: ElderFund is a discretionary scheme specifically for lower-income Singapore Citizens aged 30 and above with severe disability who:

options.A: Are NOT eligible for CareShield Life, ElderShield or IDAPE
options.B: Are covered by CareShield Life
options.C: Hold an Integrated Shield Plan
options.D: Are still working full-time

explanation: ElderFund targets those NOT eligible for CareShield Life, ElderShield or IDAPE, paying S$150 or S$250 per month. Existing CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholders are not eligible.

stem: The Migrant Domestic Worker (MDW) Levy Concession for caring for a person with disability requires that the care recipient needs help with at least:

options.A: Three of the six ADLs
options.B: Two of the six ADLs
options.C: Four of the six ADLs
options.D: One of the six ADLs

explanation: The MDW Levy Concession needs help with at least 1 ADL, lowering the levy to S$60 per month. Schemes like PioneerDAS and the Home Caregiving Grant require 3 of 6 ADLs.

stem: A policyholder receiving ElderShield 400 remains severely disabled for the full maximum benefit term. What is the total amount he receives over that period?
explanation: ESH400 pays S$400 per month for up to 72 months: S$400 x 72 = S$28,800. S$18,000 wrongly uses the ESH300 figures (S$300 x 60).

stem: Under ElderShield 300, if a claimant draws the benefit for the full maximum duration, what total payout does he receive?
explanation: ESH300 pays S$300 per month for up to 60 months: S$300 x 60 = S$18,000. S$28,800 is the ESH400 total (S$400 x 72).

stem: The original product now known as Critical Illness Insurance was first marketed under a different name and covered only a handful of conditions. Which set of conditions did that original product cover?

options.A: Cancer, Stroke, Multiple Sclerosis and Parkinson's Disease
options.B: Stroke, Heart Attack, Diabetes and Alzheimer's Disease
options.C: Cancer, Stroke, Heart Attack and Coronary Artery Bypass
options.D: Cancer, Kidney Failure, Blindness and Major Burns

explanation: The product was originally called Dread Disease Insurance and covered exactly four conditions: Cancer, Stroke, Heart Attack and Coronary Artery Bypass. The list of covered illnesses expanded greatly over time.

stem: Under the LIA Critical Illness Framework 2019, how many severe critical illnesses have standardised common definitions, and what does LIA standardise?

options.A: 30 conditions, with LIA defining all stages of severity
options.B: 36 conditions, with each insurer free to define the severe stage
options.C: 37 conditions, with LIA defining only the severe stage
options.D: 37 conditions, with LIA defining every stage from early to severe

explanation: The industry standardises common definitions for 37 severe critical illnesses. LIA defines only the severe stage; insurers set their own definitions for mildly to moderately severe or extremely severe stages and for conditions not on the list.

stem: A survival period requirement, where the life insured must stay alive for a set time after a critical illness occurs before the benefit is paid, applies to which type of critical illness cover?

options.A: Every stand-alone CI policy without exception
options.B: The Acceleration Benefit type of CI cover only
options.C: The Additional Benefit type of CI cover only
options.D: Only Multiple Pay CI plans

explanation: The survival period applies only to the Additional Benefit type of CI cover. The waiting period, by contrast, applies to CI cover generally and relates to timing of diagnosis after policy commencement.

stem: If a person is found to suffer a critical illness before or during the waiting period of a stand-alone CI policy, what does the insurer do?

options.A: Pays the full sum assured but terminates the policy
options.B: Voids the policy and refunds the premiums paid
options.C: Keeps the policy in force but excludes that one condition
options.D: Pays half the sum assured as a goodwill gesture

explanation: The waiting period prevents anti-selection. A CI diagnosed before or during the waiting period is not covered, so the insurer voids the policy and refunds premiums paid rather than paying any benefit.

stem: For a claim under the Major Cancer definition of a traditional CI policy, which of the following would NOT meet the definition?

options.A: A sarcoma with destruction of surrounding normal tissue
options.B: A lymphoma with uncontrolled growth of malignant cells
options.C: A carcinoma-in-situ classified as Tis with no invasion of normal tissue
options.D: A malignant tumour with histological confirmation and invasion of tissue

explanation: Major Cancer requires a malignant tumour with invasion and destruction of normal tissue. Pre-malignant, non-invasive and carcinoma-in-situ (Tis/Ta) classifications are specifically excluded, so an in-situ cancer with no invasion does not qualify.

stem: A S$200,000 Whole Life policy has a 50% Acceleration Benefit CI rider. The insured is diagnosed with a covered CI. What is paid on diagnosis, and what remains for a later death claim?

options.A: S$200,000 paid on CI, and the policy pays nothing further on death
options.B: S$200,000 paid on CI, with S$200,000 plus bonuses paid on later death
options.C: S$100,000 paid on CI, with S$200,000 paid on later death
options.D: S$100,000 paid on CI, with S$100,000 plus bonuses paid on later death

explanation: With acceleration the CI payout is taken out of the basic sum assured. Fifty per cent of S$200,000 is S$100,000 paid on CI, leaving S$100,000 plus bonuses for a later death or TPD claim. Total never exceeds the basic sum assured plus bonuses.

stem: A S$100,000 Whole Life policy carries a S$200,000 Additional Benefit CI rider. The insured suffers a covered CI and later dies. What is the total amount paid out?
explanation: An Additional Benefit rider pays on top of the basic policy without reducing it. The rider pays S$200,000 on CI and the S$100,000 basic sum assured is still paid on death, for a total of S$300,000.

stem: Which statement best describes a Severity-Based (Early Pay) CI plan compared to a traditional severe-only CI plan?

options.A: It pays a fixed daily cash amount regardless of the severity of illness
options.B: It pays only the full sum assured but at a cheaper premium than a severe-only plan
options.C: It pays only on the severe stage but allows unlimited repeated claims for free
options.D: It pays a percentage of the sum assured at each stage of illness and is more expensive than a severe-only plan

explanation: Severity-Based CI pays a percentage of the sum assured at early, intermediate and severe stages, allows claims at an earlier stage and more than once, and is more expensive than a traditional severe-only CI plan.

stem: Which type of CI plan allows a second and subsequent claim, including for relapse or recurrence, subject to applicable waiting periods?

options.A: A Multiple Pay CI plan
options.B: A stand-alone Term CI policy
options.C: Any Additional Benefit CI rider
options.D: A traditional Acceleration Benefit CI plan

explanation: Only Multiple Pay CI plans pay out more than once, including for relapse or recurrence. Traditional and acceleration CI plans allow only one claim.

stem: A CI plan that covers mental illness typically pays a lump sum on diagnosis of a listed condition. How many mental illness conditions are covered and how does the payout compare to the original CI amount?

options.A: Seven conditions, paying a fixed daily benefit while hospitalised
options.B: Ten conditions, paying the full original CI amount each time
options.C: Five conditions, paying a reduced sum subject to a maximum benefit per life
options.D: Three conditions, paying the full original CI amount once only

explanation: Mental illness cover is limited to exactly five conditions (Major Depressive Disorders, Schizophrenia, Bipolar Disorder, OCD and Tourette Syndrome) and pays a reduced sum, not the full original CI amount, subject to a maximum benefit per life.

stem: As a rule of thumb for adequacy, how many years of income should critical illness coverage aim to support the insured's standard of living, after taking debt into account?

options.A: At least four years of income
options.B: Exactly one year of income
options.C: At least ten years of income
options.D: At least twenty years of income

explanation: The adequacy guideline is at least four years of income, so the net coverage supports the insured's standard of living for four years while also allowing for recovery expenses and dependents.

stem: Which of the following CI arrangements does NOT acquire any cash value and therefore has no non-forfeiture option?

options.A: A CI benefit packaged into an Endowment policy
options.B: Any CI cover attached to a participating Whole Life plan
options.C: A stand-alone Term CI policy or a CI rider
options.D: A CI benefit packaged into a Whole Life policy

explanation: A stand-alone Term CI policy and a CI rider do not accumulate cash value, so no non-forfeiture option exists. Only CI packaged into Whole Life or Endowment policies builds cash value.

stem: How does Group CI Insurance differ from individual CI cover with respect to expiry age?

options.A: Group CI always specifies an expiry age even for Additional Benefit cover
options.B: Group CI has an expiry age only for Acceleration Benefit cover
options.C: Group CI never has an expiry age for any type of cover
options.D: Group CI is always whole-of-life with no expiry age

explanation: Group CI Insurance always specifies an expiry age (for example 75 years) regardless of whether it is Acceleration or Additional Benefit cover, unlike some individual whole-life CI arrangements.

stem: How does the non-medical limit for underwriting CI compare with that for Life Insurance?

options.A: The two limits are always identical
options.B: The non-medical limit for CI is higher than for Life Insurance
options.C: CI has no non-medical limit at all
options.D: The non-medical limit for CI is lower than for Life Insurance

explanation: CI underwriting is basically the same as for Life Insurance except that the non-medical limit for CI is lower, and generally only standard and sub-standard risks up to a medium rating can be accepted.

stem: How does a Hospital Cash (Hospital Income) benefit interact with a person's MediShield Life and Integrated Shield Plan payouts?

options.A: It is only paid if MediShield Life declines the claim
options.B: It is offset against those plans so there is no double recovery
options.C: It reimburses the actual hospital bill up to a daily cap
options.D: It is paid on top of those plans, unrelated to actual hospitalisation costs

explanation: Hospital Cash pays a fixed daily amount independent of actual costs and is paid on top of all other health insurance including MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans and Group H&S schemes.

stem: Under a typical Hospital Cash policy, when does a waiting period apply?

options.A: For injury, but not for illness
options.B: For both illness and accidental injury equally
options.C: For neither, since the plan has no waiting period at all
options.D: For illness, but not for injury caused directly by an accident

explanation: There is no waiting period for injury caused directly and independently by an accident, but a waiting period applies for illness. Pre-existing conditions are permanently excluded.

stem: Which feature is characteristic of a stand-alone Hospital Cash plan rather than a basic rider version?

options.A: Double or triple daily payment for ICU or overseas or accident-related stays
options.B: Coverage of pre-existing conditions from day one
options.C: Reimbursement of the actual itemised hospital bill
options.D: A guaranteed level premium that never changes with age

explanation: Stand-alone Hospital Cash plans offer enhanced multiples such as double or triple payment for ICU stays or accident or overseas hospitalisation, along with other extras. Premiums still rise by age-band on renewal.

stem: What does Maternity Insurance typically NOT cover?

options.A: The usual cost of giving birth where no complications arise
options.B: Medical expenses for covered complications of pregnancy
options.C: Congenital illnesses of the newborn
options.D: Hospitalisation income for the mother during a covered complication

explanation: Maternity Insurance covers complications of pregnancy and birth but excludes the usual cost of a normal, complication-free childbirth including its pre- and post-hospitalisation bills.

stem: Which description matches the basic structure of Maternity Insurance?

options.A: An annually renewable policy with a guaranteed cash surrender value
options.B: A regular-premium whole life policy with cash value
options.C: A single-premium term policy valid for three years with no cash value and no assignment
options.D: A single-premium policy valid for the mother's lifetime

explanation: Maternity Insurance is a single-premium term policy valid for three years from the start date, has no cash value, allows no assignment, and covers mother and child from as early as the 13th week of pregnancy.

stem: Under Travel Insurance, who decides whether an emergency medical evacuation should take place?

options.A: The airline operating the return flight
options.B: The travel agent who sold the trip
options.C: The insured person alone, at their own discretion
options.D: The attending doctor or the insurer's contracted specialist company

explanation: Evacuation is arranged when local medical services are inadequate. The decision rests with the attending doctor or the insurer's contracted specialist company reached through the 24-hour hotline, not the insured.

stem: How is Group Dental Care Insurance usually offered?

options.A: As a stand-alone individual policy requiring full medical underwriting
options.B: As a rider to a Group Hospital and Surgical policy, without underwriting
options.C: Only as part of MediShield Life
options.D: As a compulsory government scheme for all employees

explanation: Group Dental Care Insurance is issued as a rider to a Group Hospital and Surgical policy, is offered without underwriting, and covers only actively-at-work employees.

stem: What is the purpose of the Limitation Clause found in Group Dental Care Insurance?

options.A: To limit dental treatment to only the cheapest available clinics
options.B: To exclude all cover once an employee reaches age 40
options.C: To cap the number of employees that can be covered under the policy
options.D: To reduce reimbursements by amounts claimable from other sources, preventing double recovery

explanation: The Limitation Clause co-ordinates benefits by reducing payouts by amounts claimable under Work Injury Compensation, any government or public dental programme, or any other group or individual Health or Dental policy.

stem: Harry holds a Hospital Cash plan paying S$100 per day, capped at 180 days per hospitalisation and 1,000 days per lifetime, with a lifetime balance of 1,000 days still available. He is hospitalised for one continuous stay of 200 days. How much is paid for this stay?
explanation: The per-hospitalisation cap of 180 days applies even though 200 days were spent in hospital. 180 days x S$100 = S$18,000. The 20 days beyond the per-hospitalisation cap are not paid.

stem: What form of Managed Healthcare (MHC) insurance is available in Singapore?

options.A: Both individual and group MHC insurance
options.B: Neither; MHC is illegal in Singapore
options.C: Only Group MHC insurance
options.D: Only individual MHC insurance

explanation: Locally, only Group MHC insurance is available, often bought by employers as part of an Employee Benefit package and as an alternative to Group H&S plans. Individual MHC is not offered.

stem: Managed Healthcare contains and controls healthcare expenditure by managing which three components?

options.A: Accessibility, quality of care and geographic reach
options.B: Accessibility, cost and quality of care
options.C: Accessibility, cost and speed of treatment
options.D: Cost, quality of care and premium size

explanation: MHC manages three components: accessibility, cost and quality of care, achieved partly through a negotiated healthcare provider network.

stem: In most MHC plans, what is the role of the Primary Care Physician (PCP)?

options.A: A specialist who performs all surgeries for the member
options.B: An administrator who only processes claims
options.C: A gatekeeper whose referral is needed before a member sees a specialist
options.D: A physician the member may never change once assigned

explanation: The PCP is the member's first contact and personal physician. A referral from the PCP is usually required before seeing a specialist, so PCPs are called gatekeepers. Members are allowed to change their PCPs.

stem: Which MHC payment method pays the provider a fixed pre-paid amount per member each month regardless of how much the member uses services?

options.A: Fee Schedule
options.B: Capitation
options.C: Discounted-Fee-For-Service
options.D: Salary

explanation: Capitation is a fixed pre-paid amount per member, usually monthly, regardless of usage. A Fee Schedule instead caps the dollar amount reimbursed per procedure.

stem: Among managed care arrangements, which is generally the MOST restrictive with the lowest choice of provider?

options.A: Preferred Provider Organisation (PPO)
options.B: Traditional Medical Expense Insurance
options.C: Health Maintenance Organisation (HMO)
options.D: Point-of-Service (POS) plan

explanation: The HMO offers the greatest cost control but the lowest choice of provider, requiring care from network providers and a PCP referral for specialists, making it the most restrictive type.

stem: Which statement about a Preferred Provider Organisation (PPO) is correct?

options.A: A member does not need to choose a PCP or obtain a referral to see a specialist
options.B: A member is never covered for any out-of-network care
options.C: A PPO offers the least choice of provider of all plans
options.D: A member must always get a PCP referral before seeing a specialist

explanation: A PPO does not require selecting a PCP or getting referrals. It gives financial incentives to use network providers but is less restrictive than an HMO, though it usually involves greater out-of-pocket payments.

stem: A Point-of-Service (POS) plan is best described as which of the following?

options.A: A plan identical to an HMO with no out-of-network coverage at all
options.B: A hybrid combining an HMO-style referral requirement with PPO-style out-of-network coverage at higher cost
options.C: Traditional Medical Expense Insurance with no cost control
options.D: A plan identical to a PPO with no PCP and no referrals

explanation: A POS plan combines features of both: like an HMO it needs an in-network PCP and referrals, and like a PPO it still covers out-of-network care but at higher cost to the member.

stem: Ordering arrangements from greatest cost control to greatest choice of provider, which sequence is correct?

options.A: PPO, HMO, POS, then Traditional Medical Expense Insurance
options.B: HMO, POS, PPO, then Traditional Medical Expense Insurance
options.C: POS, HMO, Traditional Medical Expense Insurance, then PPO
options.D: Traditional Medical Expense Insurance, PPO, POS, then HMO

explanation: By decreasing cost control and increasing provider choice the order is HMO, POS, PPO, then Traditional Medical Expense Insurance, which has no cost control and no access restriction.

stem: Under an MHC Insurance plan, who typically needs to file a claim with the insurer?

options.A: No member ever files a claim under any circumstances
options.B: Only members who use in-network care
options.C: All members, whether in-network or out-of-network
options.D: Only members who use out-of-network care

explanation: In-network care is settled directly between the MHCO and the providers, so in-network members do not file claims. Only out-of-network members must submit a claim with the claimant's statement and original itemised bill.

stem: Which ward classes attract heavy government subsidies, and roughly what proportion of public hospital beds do they represent?

options.A: Class B2 and C, about 81% of public hospital beds
options.B: Class B2 and C, about 20% of public hospital beds
options.C: Class A and B1, about half of public hospital beds
options.D: Class A and B1, about 81% of public hospital beds

explanation: Class B2 and C admissions make up about 81% of public hospital beds and are heavily subsidised (50% to 80% for Singapore Citizens). Class A and B1 patients receive little to no subsidy.

stem: With effect from November 2019, how did eligibility for the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) change?

options.A: It was expanded to include all Singapore Citizens regardless of income
options.B: It was extended to cover all Permanent Residents
options.C: It was restricted to Pioneer Generation seniors only
options.D: It was closed to new applicants entirely

explanation: From November 2019 CHAS was expanded to include all Singapore Citizens regardless of income, with card colours (Blue, Orange, Green) indicating the subsidy tier.

stem: MediShield Life claim limits are designed to fully cover how many subsidised bills, and for which ward class in particular?

options.A: 7 in 10 subsidised bills, for private hospital stays
options.B: 9 in 10 subsidised bills, for Class B2/C ward hospitalisation
options.C: 10 in 10 subsidised bills, for Class A ward hospitalisation
options.D: 9 in 10 subsidised bills, for Class B1 ward hospitalisation

explanation: MediShield Life is sized to cover 9 in 10 subsidised bills for Class B2/C ward hospitalisation, day surgeries and selected costly outpatient treatments. Those wanting higher-ward or private cover need an Integrated Shield Plan.

stem: Under MediShield Life, an Additional Premium applies to which policyholders, and at what rate and duration?

options.A: Those with any pre-existing condition, at 50% for the first 5 years
options.B: Those with serious pre-existing conditions listed by MOH, at 30% for the first 10 years
options.C: Permanent Residents only, at 30% for the first 3 years
options.D: All policyholders above age 65, at 30% for life

explanation: Only those with serious pre-existing conditions listed by MOH pay an Additional Premium of 30% for the first 10 years of coverage, on top of standard premiums. Everyone else pays standard premiums.

stem: The MediShield Life premium subsidy for lower- to middle-income households provides up to what percentage of premiums for Singapore Citizens?

options.A: Up to 50% of premiums
options.B: Up to 30% of premiums
options.C: Up to 75% of premiums
options.D: Up to 100% of premiums

explanation: Income-based premium subsidies provide up to 50% of premiums for eligible lower- to middle-income Singapore Citizens; Permanent Residents receive half the Singapore Citizen subsidy.

stem: A person receiving Additional Premium Support (APS) for MediShield Life would LOSE that support if they do what?

options.A: Purchase an Integrated Shield Plan or an ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement
options.B: Move to a heavily subsidised Class C ward
options.C: Apply for a CHAS card
options.D: Continue to pay their standard MediShield Life premiums by MediSave

explanation: APS covers outstanding premiums plus the next two years' premiums, but a person loses APS if they buy an Integrated Shield Plan or an ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement, since these signal ability to afford additional cover.

stem: In the MediShield Life claim process, when is pro-ration applied to a Class A/B1 or private hospital bill?

options.A: Only after the maximum annual claim limit is reached
options.B: After the deductible and co-insurance have already been deducted
options.C: Never; pro-ration applies only to outpatient bills
options.D: Before the claim limits, deductible and co-insurance are applied, reducing the bill to the Class B2/C equivalent

explanation: Higher-ward and private bills are pro-rated down to the equivalent Class B2/C level first, before claim limits, deductible and co-insurance are applied. This ensures comparable payouts for subsidised and private patients.

stem: According to Appendix 9B (updated April 2024), what is the MediShield Life daily claim limit for a Normal Ward and the maximum claim limit per policy year?

options.A: S$700 per day and S$150,000 per policy year
options.B: S$700 per day and S$100,000 per policy year
options.C: S$800 per day and S$100,000 per policy year
options.D: S$800 per day and S$150,000 per policy year

explanation: Appendix 9B (April 2024) gives the Normal Ward daily limit as S$800 per day and the maximum claim limit as S$150,000 per policy year with no lifetime limit. An older worked example used S$700 per day, but the appendix figure is authoritative.

stem: Under MediShield Life, the co-insurance rate applied to the claimable amount accumulated within a policy year is tiered how?

options.A: A flat 10% on the entire claimable amount
options.B: 3% on the first S$5,000, 5% on the next S$5,000, and 10% above S$10,000
options.C: 5% on the first S$10,000 and 3% thereafter
options.D: 10% on the first S$5,000, 5% on the next S$5,000, and 3% above S$10,000

explanation: Co-insurance decreases as the bill grows: 10% on the first S$5,000 (inclusive of the deductible), 5% on the next S$5,000, and 3% above S$10,000. Outpatient co-insurance is a flat 10%.

stem: Which of the following is NOT covered by MediShield Life for admissions on or after 1 March 2021?

options.A: Overseas medical treatment
options.B: Kidney dialysis as an approved outpatient treatment
options.C: Approved inpatient surgical procedures in a Class C ward
options.D: Selected costly cancer drug treatments

explanation: MediShield Life excludes overseas medical treatment, along with vaccination, ambulance services and expenses after the 7th day from being certified fit for discharge. It does cover local approved surgeries, dialysis and cancer drug treatments.

stem: An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is made up of two parts. What are they?

options.A: A MediSave component and a CareShield Life component
options.B: Two independent private insurance components from two different insurers
options.C: A CHAS component and a MediFund component
options.D: A MediShield Life component administered by the CPF Board, plus an additional private insurance component

explanation: An IP combines the MediShield Life component administered by the CPF Board with an additional private insurance component from an approved private insurer, typically covering Class A/B1 or private hospitals. There is one premium and one claim, with no duplication.

stem: For a person holding an Integrated Shield Plan, how are pre-existing conditions treated under the MediShield Life component?

options.A: They are covered only if the private insurer chooses to accept them
options.B: They are excluded from both the MediShield Life and the private component
options.C: They are covered only for the first 10 years of the plan
options.D: They remain covered with lifelong protection even if excluded from the private component

explanation: The MediShield Life component gives lifelong coverage and covers all pre-existing conditions, even if the private insurance component of the IP excludes that condition.

stem: The Standard Integrated Shield Plan targets which ward class, and how do its benefits compare across insurers?

options.A: Private hospitals, with benefits set independently by each insurer
options.B: Class A, with benefits identical across insurers including premiums
options.C: Class B1, with benefits regulated by MOH and identical across all IP insurers
options.D: Class B2/C, with benefits that differ freely between insurers

explanation: The Standard IP is a no-frills product covering large Class B1 ward bills, with benefits regulated by MOH and identical across all IP insurers. Premiums and underwriting, however, are still set by each insurer.

stem: For new Integrated Shield Plan riders introduced from 8 March 2018, what minimum co-payment is required, and can the rider premium be paid using MediSave?

options.A: At least 10% co-payment, and the rider is MediSave-payable up to the AWL
options.B: No co-payment at all, and the rider is fully MediSave-payable
options.C: At least 5% co-payment, and the rider is not MediSave-approved (cash only)
options.D: At least 5% co-payment, and the rider is fully MediSave-payable

explanation: New IP riders must have a co-payment of 5% or more, and riders are not MediSave-approved, so they can be paid in cash only. Full riders that covered the entire co-payment are no longer allowed.

stem: A policyholder switches their Integrated Shield Plan to a new insurer, then changes their mind. Within how many days can they revert to the previous insurer without re-underwriting?

options.A: Within 14 days of the termination notification
options.B: Within 30 days of the termination notification
options.C: Within 90 days of the termination notification
options.D: Within 60 days of the termination notification

explanation: Switching insurers triggers new underwriting, but there is a 30-day window from the termination notification to revert to the previous insurer with no re-underwriting, as if the first IP was never terminated.

stem: When was MediSave, the national health savings scheme under the CPF, introduced?

options.A: 1 April 1984
options.B: 1 January 2009
options.C: 1 November 2015
options.D: 30 September 2002

explanation: MediSave was introduced on 1 April 1984 as a mandatory national health savings scheme under the CPF. (1 November 2015 is when MediShield Life started, and September 2002 is when ElderShield launched.)

stem: What happens to the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) once a CPF member reaches age 65?

options.A: It doubles automatically to fund old-age care
options.B: It is reset to zero and rebuilt from scratch
options.C: It continues to be raised every January like everyone else
options.D: It is fixed for the rest of the member's life and no longer adjusted

explanation: The BHS is adjusted yearly in January only for members aged 65 and below that year. Once a member reaches age 65 the BHS is fixed for the rest of their life.

stem: Under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), MediSave can pay for outpatient treatment of approved chronic conditions up to what annual limits?

options.A: S$300 for non-complex or S$500 for complex chronic conditions per patient per year
options.B: S$500 for non-complex or S$700 for complex chronic conditions per patient per year
options.C: A flat S$400 per patient per year regardless of complexity
options.D: S$700 for non-complex or S$900 for complex chronic conditions per patient per year

explanation: The MediSave500/700 limits allow up to S$500 for non-complex chronic conditions or S$700 for complex chronic conditions per patient per year for the 23 approved CDMP conditions.

stem: For an Integrated Shield Plan claim, the IP insurer computes the IP payout and the CPF Board independently computes the MediShield Life payout. What is the eventual payout?

options.A: The average of the two amounts
options.B: The higher of the two computed amounts
options.C: The sum of both amounts added together
options.D: The lower of the two computed amounts

explanation: To avoid duplication, the eventual payout is the higher of the IP benefit and the MediShield Life benefit, not the sum. The MOH claims order is third party or employer first, then MediShield Life/IP, then MediSave, then cash.

stem: How does ElderShield differ from MediShield Life in terms of enrolment?

options.A: Both are voluntary opt-in schemes
options.B: ElderShield is an opt-out scheme, whereas MediShield Life is compulsory
options.C: ElderShield is compulsory, whereas MediShield Life is opt-out
options.D: Both are compulsory with automatic enrolment

explanation: Unlike compulsory MediShield Life, ElderShield is an opt-out scheme. ElderShield became a closed scheme from 1 August 2021, with the Government taking over administration from 1 November 2021.

stem: To qualify for an ElderShield payout, the insured must be unable to perform at least how many of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)?

options.A: All six of the ADLs
options.B: At least three of the six ADLs
options.C: At least two of the six ADLs
options.D: At least one of the six ADLs

explanation: ElderShield (like CareShield Life) pays when the insured cannot perform at least three of the six ADLs: Washing, Dressing, Feeding, Toileting, Mobility and Transferring.

stem: In ElderShield, how do the waiting period and the deferment period differ?

options.A: The waiting period runs from the claim date, while the deferment period runs from commencement
options.B: The waiting period runs 90 days from commencement, while the deferment period runs 90 days from the claim date
options.C: Both run from the date cover commences
options.D: Both run from the date the claim is received by the AIC

explanation: The waiting period is 90 days from commencement (disability in the first 90 days terminates the policy with premiums refunded), while the deferment period is 90 days from the claim date, after which the benefit is payable if the insured is still disabled.

stem: What is the entry age range for ElderShield?

options.A: Minimum entry age 40, maximum entry age 64
options.B: Minimum entry age 30, no maximum entry age
options.C: Minimum entry age 50, maximum entry age 70
options.D: Minimum entry age 21, maximum entry age 55

explanation: ElderShield has a minimum entry age of 40 and a maximum entry age of 64, with a 75-day grace period and a 60-day free-look period. CareShield Life, by contrast, covers from age 30.

stem: CareShield Life is compulsory for Singapore Citizens and PRs born in which years, and from what age are they automatically covered?

options.A: Born 1979 or earlier, covered automatically from age 40
options.B: Born 1990 or later, covered automatically from age 21
options.C: Born 1970 or earlier, covered automatically from age 65
options.D: Born 1980 or later, covered automatically from age 30

explanation: CareShield Life is universal and compulsory for those born in 1980 or later, who are automatically covered on their 30th birthday or the October 2020 launch, whichever is later. Those born 1979 or earlier may opt in.

stem: How does the payout duration of CareShield Life compare with that of ElderShield?

options.A: Both schemes pay for the insured's entire lifetime with no cap
options.B: CareShield Life pays for a maximum of 60 months, like ElderShield300
options.C: CareShield Life pays for as long as severe disability persists with no duration cap, unlike ElderShield's 60 or 72-month limits
options.D: CareShield Life pays for a maximum of 72 months, the same as ElderShield400

explanation: CareShield Life pays at least S$600 per month for as long as the insured has severe disability, with no cap on payout duration. ElderShield, by contrast, is capped at 60 months (ElderShield300) or 72 months (ElderShield400).

stem: To qualify for the Pioneer Generation Package, a Singaporean must have been born on or before which date and obtained citizenship by which date?

options.A: Born between 1960 and 1973 and a citizen on or before 31 December 1996
options.B: Born on or before 31 December 1949 and a citizen on or before 31 December 1986
options.C: Born on or before 31 December 1959 and a citizen on or before 31 December 1986
options.D: Born between 1950 and 1959 and a citizen on or before 31 December 1996

explanation: Pioneer Generation members were aged 16 and above in 1965 (born on or before 31 December 1949) and obtained citizenship on or before 31 December 1986. Those born 1950 to 1959 fall under the Merdeka Generation.

stem: How much of the remaining subsidised bill at polyclinics and SOCs do Merdeka Generation seniors receive off, compared with Pioneer Generation seniors?

options.A: Merdeka gets an additional 50% off, while Pioneer gets an additional 25% off
options.B: Merdeka gets an additional 25% off, while Pioneer gets an additional 50% off
options.C: Both get an additional 25% off
options.D: Both get an additional 50% off

explanation: Merdeka Generation seniors receive an additional 25% off remaining subsidised bills at polyclinics and SOCs, whereas Pioneer Generation seniors receive an additional 50% off.

stem: IDAPE (Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly) provides a monthly payout for up to 72 months. What are the payout amounts by per capita household income (PCHI)?

options.A: S$600 per month regardless of PCHI
options.B: S$250 per month for PCHI up to S$2,000, or S$150 per month for PCHI S$2,001 to S$2,800
options.C: S$300 per month for PCHI up to S$2,000, or S$250 per month for PCHI S$2,001 to S$2,800
options.D: S$400 per month for PCHI up to S$2,000, or S$300 per month for PCHI S$2,001 to S$2,800

explanation: From 1 July 2013, IDAPE pays S$250 per month (up to 72 months) for PCHI of S$0 to S$2,000, and S$150 per month for PCHI of S$2,001 to S$2,800. These amounts are lower than ElderShield payouts.

stem: ElderFund is a discretionary assistance scheme. Who is its target group and what is the maximum monthly amount?

options.A: Any citizen regardless of income or disability, up to S$1,000 per month
options.B: Lower-income Singapore Citizens aged 30 and older with severe disability who cannot benefit from CareShield Life, ElderShield or IDAPE, up to S$250 per month
options.C: Permanent Residents with severe disability, up to S$400 per month
options.D: All Singapore Citizens aged 65 and older, up to S$600 per month

explanation: ElderFund is a discretionary safety net for lower-income Singapore Citizens aged 30 and older with severe disability who fall outside CareShield Life, ElderShield and IDAPE, providing up to S$250 per month.

stem: MediFund is the final safety net in Singapore's healthcare financing. Which statement about how it is funded and disbursed is correct?

options.A: It is an endowment fund from which only the interest income is disbursed, after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave
options.B: It is funded by MediShield Life premiums and pays before MediSave is used
options.C: It disburses both the capital and interest to any applicant on request
options.D: It is a private insurance fund that pays before government subsidies apply

explanation: MediFund is an endowment fund; only the interest income from the capital sum is allocated to approved institutions. It is the final safety net after government subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave, and applicants must be subsidised Singapore Citizen patients.

stem: The MediShield Life component of an IP premium is fully MediSave-payable. For the additional private insurance component, MediSave use is capped by the Additional Withdrawal Limit (AWL). What is the AWL for an insured aged 55 (Age Next Birthday)?

options.A: S$600 per policy year
